## Overview

Camera-trap monitoring networks may use the same data standard but follow different analytical methods, parameter settings, and reporting conventions. In `camtrapReport`, **analytical profiles** bring these choices together into reusable workflows tailored to each monitoring context.

A profile defines which analytical and reporting modules are used and how they are organised. This allows monitoring networks and individual projects to apply a consistent workflow across datasets, sites, and repeated surveys, while sharing analytical components where appropriate.

Profiles do not contain the data or analytical code. They reference existing modules and their configurations, making it easier to reuse established workflows without rebuilding them for each study.

### Explore available profiles

`camtrapReport` provides a **default analytical profile** for camera-trap reporting. It also supports network-specific profiles that bring together agreed analytical methods, parameter settings, and reporting conventions into reusable, reproducible workflows. This helps monitoring networks apply consistent analyses across datasets, sites, and repeated surveys, while contributing to a growing **shared knowledge hub of standardised analytical workflows** that other networks and projects can adopt, adapt, and improve.

For example, the **[European Observatory of Wildlife (EOW)](https://wildlifeobservatory.org/)** profile is designed around the analytical choices agreed upon within the network. Methods such as the Random Encounter Model (REM) involve several parameters and assumptions that can substantially influence density estimates. Even small differences in how these are applied can affect results and make comparisons across sites or years difficult. By defining these choices within a shared profile, networks can apply a consistent workflow suited to their monitoring objectives, improving the reproducibility and comparability of results.

```{r explore-profiles, eval=FALSE}
library(camtrapReport)

# Generate an EOW ecological report
report(
  cm,
  profile = "EOW",
  filename = "EOW-report",
  format = "pdf",
  view = FALSE
)
```

The EOW profile illustrates how a monitoring-specific workflow can be implemented in `camtrapReport`. Its inclusion does not necessarily indicate formal endorsement by the EOW network.

## Create and use a profile

You can create a profile by selecting the ecological and data-status modules that suit your monitoring objectives.

```{r create-profile, eval=FALSE}
project <- reportProfile(
  name = "project",
  description = "Our monitoring workflow",
  report = c("introduction", "methods"),
  status = c("spatial", "temporal", "availability")
)

add_profile(cm, project)

# Use the profile for both reports
report(cm, profile = "project")
status(cm, profile = "project")
```

## Share and reuse profiles

Profiles can be saved as YAML files and shared with other researchers or monitoring networks.

```{r share-profile, eval=FALSE}
# Save a profile
write_profile("project", "project-profile.yml", object = cm)

# Reuse it with another dataset
shared_profile <- read_profile("project-profile.yml")
add_profile(other_cm, shared_profile)
```

Shared profiles reference existing analytical modules, so the receiving project must have the required modules available. For reproducibility, retain the profile alongside its configurations, input data, and software versions.

See the [Module management guide](https://spatialecology.github.io/camtrapReport/articles/modules.html) for customising modules and report sections.

## Contribute a profile

Monitoring networks and individual projects can contribute profiles documenting their analytical and reporting workflows.

Our aim is to develop a shared library of analytical profiles that researchers can inspect, reuse, and adapt. Over time, this could become a knowledge hub of documented analytical practices, helping monitoring communities share methodological expertise and develop more consistent reporting workflows.

Interested in contributing? [Open a GitHub issue](https://github.com/spatialecology/camtrapReport/issues) to describe your monitoring objectives, analytical methods, and reporting requirements. Profiles and any required modules can then be developed and reviewed together.
